title: Mindset: The New Psychology of Success
author: Carol S. Dweck
tagline: How a fixed or growth mindset shapes learning, work, sport and relationships.
overview: Dweck's research shows that people with a fixed mindset believe abilities are set, while people with a growth mindset believe abilities can be developed through effort, strategy and help. The growth mindset leads to resilience, learning and achievement — and it can be learned.

chapters.title: The Mindsets
chapters.summary: Dweck introduces two mindsets. In the fixed mindset, qualities like intelligence are carved in stone, so every task becomes a test of worth. In the growth mindset, qualities can be cultivated through effort, so challenges are chances to grow.
keyIdeas: Mindset shapes how we face challenges.
chapters.tryThis: Notice one thought this week that sounds like a fixed mindset.

quiz.question: What does the growth mindset believe?
quiz.explanation: Qualities grow through effort and learning.

chapters.title: Inside the Mindsets
chapters.summary: Fixed-mindset people avoid challenges, see effort as a sign of low ability and feel threatened by others' success. Growth-mindset people embrace challenges, persist after setbacks and learn from criticism. Failure means something very different in each.
keyIdeas: Effort is the path to mastery.
chapters.tryThis: Reframe a recent failure as 'what did this teach me?'

quiz.question: How does the fixed mindset view effort?
options: As a sign of low ability
quiz.explanation: If you need effort, it suggests you aren't 'naturally' good.

chapters.title: The Truth About Ability and Accomplishment
chapters.summary: Many accomplished people weren't seen as gifted early on; their achievements came from persistent, focused effort. Praising intelligence can push students toward a fixed mindset, while praising effort and strategy encourages growth.
keyIdeas: Accomplishment comes from effort over time.
chapters.tryThis: Praise someone's strategy or effort instead of their intelligence.

quiz.question: What kind of praise encourages a growth mindset?

chapters.title: Sports: The Mindset of a Champion
chapters.summary: Natural talent alone doesn't make champions. Athletes with a growth mindset find success in learning and improving, take responsibility for setbacks and keep developing, while 'naturals' with a fixed mindset may coast and crumble under pressure.
chapters.tryThis: After your next game or task, list one thing to practise.

quiz.question: What does Dweck say makes champions?

chapters.title: Business: Mindset and Leadership
chapters.summary: Fixed-mindset leaders need to prove they're superior, surround themselves with yes-people and often fail to adapt. Growth-mindset leaders keep learning, welcome bad news and develop their teams, building organisations that last.
chapters.tryThis: Ask your team for one piece of honest negative feedback.

quiz.question: How do growth-mindset leaders treat bad news?

chapters.title: Relationships: Mindsets in Love (or Not)
chapters.summary: In relationships, a fixed mindset expects things to work effortlessly and assigns blame when problems appear. A growth mindset accepts that good relationships take work, communication and mutual development.
chapters.tryThis: Have one honest conversation about how to improve a relationship.

quiz.question: What does the growth mindset expect in relationships?
quiz.explanation: Growth comes through effort and communication.

chapters.title: Parents, Teachers, and Coaches: Where Do Mindsets Come From?
chapters.summary: The messages adults send — through praise, criticism and reactions to failure — shape children's mindsets. Great teachers and coaches set high standards in a nurturing atmosphere and teach that effort and strategy lead to improvement.
chapters.tryThis: React to someone's mistake with 'what will you try next?'

quiz.question: What combination do great teachers use?
options: High standards and a nurturing atmosphere

chapters.title: Changing Mindsets
chapters.summary: Mindsets can change. Learning how the brain grows with practice helps people adopt a growth mindset. The process involves recognising your fixed-mindset triggers, naming that inner voice and choosing a growth response — repeatedly, over time.
chapters.tryThis: Give your fixed-mindset voice a name and talk back to it once this week.

quiz.question: Can mindsets change?
quiz.explanation: Dweck shows mindsets can be learned.
